name: ROI-First Readable Ad Typography
use_when: A UGC, coaching, product, or direct-response ad needs text that sells the claim quickly.
A client reference asks for typography but the edit still has to optimize comprehension and CTA clarity.
The agent must choose between artistic typography and clean performance text.
avoid_when: The deliverable is an art film, music video, or brand mood piece where typography is intentionally expressive.
The client's approved brand system requires a more stylized treatment.
The screen already communicates the product/result without extra text.

timeline_pattern.pattern: ad_goal -> product_or_result_claim -> client_reference -> clean_type_layout -> proof_or_cta_priority -> readability_qc -> variant_test
timeline_pattern.goal_rule: For performance ads, prioritize the product, result, objection, offer, and CTA before decorative type choices.
timeline_pattern.reference_rule: Use client references to match the style lane, then simplify anything that slows reading.
timeline_pattern.cta_rule: CTA text should be visible, short, and separated from captions or proof labels.

motion.rule: Use restrained text motion that supports the offer or proof; avoid animation that delays the claim.

keyframe_values.claim_read: The main claim should be readable in the first few seconds when it is part of the hook.
keyframe_values.cta_hold: Hold CTA text long enough to read after the product/result proof appears.

sound.rule: SFX can mark offer or proof reveals only when speech and product clarity remain dominant.

captions.rule: Do not let captions, offer text, and CTA compete; assign each a clear role and screen region.

color.rule: Use brand or comparison colors only if they improve product/result comprehension; avoid low-contrast premium styling on claims.

implementation.ffmpeg: Render claim, proof, and CTA text as separate timed layers and generate phone-size contact sheets for readability.
implementation.remotion: Model adText blocks with role=claim/proof/objection/cta, priority, safeRegion, and variantId fields.
implementation.blender: Use simple title cards or product-adjacent 3D text only when it does not delay the offer.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use clean text templates, short phrases, and manual placement; simplify fancy templates when the product/result claim slows down.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Essential Graphics text roles for claim, proof, and CTA, then A/B a cleaner variant against any highly stylized reference.

common_mistakes: Making ad text artistic but slow to read.
Letting CTA text fight with subtitles or product proof.
Using a trendy font that mismatches the product category.
Copying a client reference without checking whether the claim is still clear.
Adding shadows, gradients, or effects that make the offer look cheaper or harder to read.
qc: Is the product, result, or offer readable before decorative style is noticed?
Does the CTA have a clear screen region and enough hold time?
Do captions, proof labels, and offer text avoid collision?
Does the type style match the client reference without sacrificing comprehension?
Would a cleaner text variant likely improve performance clarity?
